meaning.architrave: Always 1. Marks the JSON as a style record.
meaning.label: The name on the tile.
meaning.base: The built-in style this record starts from; every key left out rests on it. See examples for what each base is.
meaning.palette: The colour pair (a light and a dark side designed together). colours overrides its paper, ink and accent.
meaning.reading: The reading size step of the article, a fluid rung and not a pixel value; default is about 22px on a desktop. Do not set a size for a monospaced reading face, its phone floor is handled by the theme.
meaning.face: The font of the article body.
meaning.sans: The font of the interface: the rail, buttons, menus.
meaning.leading: Line spacing of the article, from solid (tightest) to loosest; default is 1.6.
meaning.dropcap: A large initial on the first paragraph; capLines is its height in lines.
meaning.capLines: Height of the initial in lines. Only with dropcap.
meaning.rounded: Rounded corners on cards, buttons and pictures. false is square.
meaning.lines: Hairlines around cards, buttons and fields and between rows. false means no lines anywhere except link underlines.
meaning.line: Strength of those lines: the ink's share in the line colour, in per cent. 45 is the rest. Only with lines.
meaning.corners: medium, small or large corners. One step re-cuts every corner together; nested corners stay sums. Only with rounded.
meaning.dots: A fine grid of dots on the page ground, a cutting mat.
meaning.dotsize: The dot grid's spacing in pixels: 16 (fine), 24 or 32 (wide). 24 is the rest. Only with dots.
meaning.dotlevel: Strength of the dots: the ink's share in the dot colour, in per cent: 6, 9, 13, 18 or 24. 13 is the rest. Only with dots.
meaning.marker: A highlighter: marked words and selected text get a wash in the marker colour, and a short bar stands under the article title. Decoration only, never a text colour.
meaning.markercolour: The highlighter's colour: yellow, green, pink, blue, orange, text (the reading text's colour), muted (the date's colour), or own (the well colours.<side>.marker, fitted to the other side's paper when set on one side only; its ink and bar follow from the pen). Only with marker.
meaning.measure: Line length of the reading text in letters: 60 to 88 in steps of 4. 72 is the rest.
meaning.space: The space of the page: xcompact, compact, standard, spacious or xspacious. Standard is the rest, the theme's own. Each kind of gap moves by its own amount: inside a group a little, between items more, between sections most, so what belongs together stays together. The reading text of an article keeps its own rhythm.
meaning.framewidth: Width of the frame around pictures in pixels: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32. 8 is the rest. Only with pictureframe.
meaning.framepattern: What the frame around pictures shows: plain, dots (the dot grid) or checker (a transparency checkerboard). Only with pictureframe.
meaning.widehead: The article's title, categories and date line stand as wide as the wide top picture, so a big title needs fewer lines; the text keeps its column.
meaning.widepicture: The article's top picture stands wider than the text column, as wide as the paper allows.
meaning.fullpicture: While the top picture is wide (widepicture), on stretches it edge to edge across the paper as a low banner (21:9, square corners). Off (the rest) keeps it wide.
meaning.categories: Where the line of categories stands on the article and on its cards: below the title (the rest), above it, or hidden. It replaced the switch kickerabove.
meaning.kickerabove: Retired 2026-09-27 and still read: true becomes categories above.
meaning.button: What fills the main buttons: accent (the rest), ink, or own (colours.<side>.button). The links keep the accent either way.
meaning.inkbutton: Retired 2026-09-26 and still read: true becomes button ink.
meaning.buttonshape: The buttons' and hover pills' corner: cards (the corner size's own, the rest), square, rounded (8 px) or pill. Only with rounded. The cards keep the corner size.
meaning.tagsfollow: The tags take the buttons' corner instead of staying round.
meaning.buttonstyle: How the main buttons look: filled (the rest), outlined, shadow (outlined with a hard shadow), tinted, gray or text (text only), in the button colour where it has one.
meaning.buttonmedium: How the other buttons (the gray secondary ones) look: gray (the rest), filled, tinted, outlined, shadow (outlined with a hard shadow) or text (text only), in the button colour where it has one.
meaning.buttonquiet: How the quiet buttons (small actions without a fill) look: text (the rest), filled, tinted, gray, outlined or shadow (outlined with a hard shadow). Architrave's alone; another theme has no quiet kind.
meaning.tags: How the tags at the end of an article look: text (the rest: words, as the theme sets them), or small pills that are filled, tinted, gray or outlined, made from the button colour. Tags follow the buttons gives the pills the buttons' corner.
meaning.chosenitem: How the chosen item is marked, the page you are on in the menu and the open tab: gray (the rest: the theme's own mark), filled with the button colour, outlined in it, or bold and underlined.
meaning.linewidth: Line width in px: 1 (the rest), 2, 3 or 5. Only with lines; fine lines only at 1.
meaning.cards: How cards look: box (the rest: the card's fill and, with lines, its line), top (a line along the top only, no fill, square; only with lines), flat (the fill alone, no line) or raised (the paper, lifted by a shadow).
meaning.quotes: How quotes in an article look: a line at the side (the rest), plain, or in a box.
meaning.notes: How a box the writer coloured inside an article looks: flat (the rest: its fill), outlined, or raised by a shadow.
meaning.fields: How search, comment and sign-up fields look: flat (the rest: the fill, with lines its line), outlined on the paper, or raised by a shadow.
meaning.titlefinish: How the title and the headings are drawn: flat (the rest: their colour), shine (from the full colour to half of it, top left to bottom right, as brushed metal) or accent (from their colour into the accent).
meaning.headitalics: The face of the serif words in titles and headings (which words: effects.serif): same (the rest: no serif), serif (Newsreader), classic (Libre Baskerville), vollkorn (Vollkorn) or fraunces (Fraunces).
meaning.headarrival: How the title and the article's headings come into view: none (the rest: they are simply there), fade (word by word) or blur (word by word, from a blur to sharp). Nothing moves for readers who ask for less motion.
meaning.cardlight: Light on the cards: off (the rest), edge (a thin light along the top edge that dies out toward the corners) or glow (the edge and a faint light falling into the card). The ink by night, the accent by day.
meaning.buttonfinish: A finish over the main and other buttons: flat (the rest: their look as set), glass (a faint sheet of the ink with a hairline) or glow (the main button keeps its fill and gets a soft light of the button colour under it; the other buttons glass).
meaning.toppattern: A pattern on the head of the paper that fades out before the reading begins: none (the rest), dots, grid, cross (small crosses) or diagonal lines.
meaning.guides: Lines down each side of the article, a gutter out, as on a drawing board: off (the rest), solid or dashed. Not on a phone.
meaning.greytint: How much of the accent the paper, the grounds and every grey take, in percent: 0 (the rest), 5, 10 or 15. The ink itself stays as it is. Only with the style's own colour pair.
meaning.pageglow: Two slow glows of the accent behind the article's title: off (the rest), soft or strong. They stay still for readers who ask for less motion.
meaning.movinglight: A short streak of the accent that travels along the top edge of the cards: off (the rest) or on. Not for readers who ask for less motion.
meaning.monitorframe: A black bezel around the page with rounded corners, an old monitor's frame: off (the rest), thin, medium or thick.
meaning.fringe: A colour fringe on every letter, the three guns of a tube not quite meeting: off (the rest), faint, soft, strong, slip (print's one magenta ghost on all text) or sliptitle (that ghost on the titles and headings only, the reading left sharp).
meaning.crisp: Letters drawn without smoothing, the stair-step of an old screen: off (the rest), headings, or all text.
meaning.scanstyle: How the scan lines are drawn: lines (the rest), grille (the RGB stripes of an aperture grille) or both. Only with scanlines.
meaning.shimmer: The screen's brightness moving: off (the rest), soft (a slow hum) or roll (a faint band drifting down). Still for readers who ask for less motion.
meaning.warp: The page bent like a tube's glass: off (the rest), slight, bulged or strong. The page is redrawn as a picture, so text softens a little.
meaning.switchon: The screen collapses to a line and blinks back when the side changes: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.bloom: The glow spilling into the paper, not only round the letters: off (the rest), soft or strong. By night only.
meaning.ghosting: A vertical smear while the page scrolls, the phosphor fading: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.jitter: The picture nudges sideways for a moment now and then, a bad sync: off (the rest), rare or often.
meaning.graincrawl: The grain standing still (the rest) or moving, as a tube's noise crawls. Only with grain.
meaning.typedtitle: The article's title arrives letter by letter behind a block cursor: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.bootscreen: A start screen on the first visit of a session, then the page: off (the rest), on (a computer's boot screen: the site's name, its line and a bar of blocks) or card (a television's test card with the site's name on its plate).
meaning.roomglass: A window reflected across the top corner of the glass: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.phosphor: The whole night screen in one phosphor: off (the rest, the style's own colours), blue, green, amber, white or black.
meaning.static: A burst of noise while the set switches on: off (the rest) or on. Only with switchon.
meaning.dropout: The title in the paper's colour on a block of ink, a headline over a photograph: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.headrule: A rule under the title: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.ink: Print bleeds a hair: sharp (the rest) or spread, the letters a little softer and heavier.
meaning.tooth: A coarser grain, the tooth of magazine stock: off (the rest) or on.
meaning.edges: The vignette's colour: ink (the rest) or yellowed, an old page's brown.
meaning.columns: The article's sections in columns: 1 (the rest), 2 or 3. Each heading with its text balances into its columns and the next starts below; one column on a phone.
meaning.paragraphs: Paragraphs spaced apart (the rest) or indented with no space between, as print sets them.
meaning.rainbow: Six rainbow stripes: off (the rest), rule (on the dividers), mark (a small square before the site's name), both, or logo (the stripes fill the site's logo itself; for a logo on a transparent ground).
meaning.postband: What stands between two posts on a page of posts: off (the rest, the theme's own gap), rainbow (the six stripes across the whole paper) or logo (the stripes with the site's logo small in a gap at their middle).
meaning.footband: What closes the page at its very foot: off (the rest), on (the six rainbow stripes as a taller band) or plate (a black plate across the paper: the site's logo and name, its tagline and the copyright line, with a faint colour fringe, the last card of a film).
meaning.menuline: The side column's menu links: plain (the rest) or underlined in the ink, as a printed page sets its navigation.
meaning.legalline: A small italic line at the foot of the page, an advertisement's small print: the copyright sign, the year, the site's name and its tagline. Only words the site already has. Off (the rest) or on.
meaning.stripes: How the rainbow bands between posts and at the page foot are drawn: solid (the rest, six stripes edge to edge) or gaps (six thinner stripes with paper between them, in softer hues).
meaning.sitename: The site's name in the side column and on the plate: plain (the rest, as the interface sets it) or caps (bold italic capitals set tight, in the section titles' face, as an advertisement's wordmark).
meaning.pillbuttons: Retired 2026-09-26 and still read: true becomes buttonshape pill.
meaning.centretitle: Retired 2026-09-25 and still read: true becomes roles.head.align and roles.kicker.align center, with roles.head.members.sub.align default.
meaning.fadeedges: which edges of the top picture fade with picturefade: sides (bottom and sides), bottom, or all four.
meaning.linestyle: solid, dashed or dotted lines. Dashes are long only when rounded is false. Only with lines.
meaning.fills: Tinted fills on cards, buttons and fields. With lines and fills both false, controls are plain glyphs.
meaning.fill: Strength of the fills as a percentage of the colour pair's own steps; 100 is the rest. Only with fills.
meaning.scanlines: Faint horizontal lines over the whole page, an old screen.
meaning.scan: Strength of the scan lines, 1 to 10 (opacity in hundredths). 3 is the rest. Only with scanlines.
meaning.glow: A soft light around the letters in their own colour. Shows on the dark side only.
meaning.glowlevel: Strength of the glow, 1 to 10. 4 is the rest. Only with glow.
meaning.grain: A fine film grain over the whole page, the tooth of paper.
meaning.softlevel: How far the reading text steps toward the paper, in percent: 10 to 45 in steps of 5. 15 is the rest. Only with soft.
meaning.quietlevel: How far the small text (dates, captions, meta) steps toward the paper with soft on, in percent: 25 to 50 in steps of 5. 25 is the rest. Only with soft, and only while smallsoft is not set; the row Small text writes smallsoft since 2026-09-27.
meaning.smallsoft: How far the small text (dates, captions, meta) steps toward the paper, in percent: 25 to 50 in steps of 5, with soft on or off. 25 is the rest, the pair's own rung. Not set, it follows quietlevel while soft is on, and an export leaves it out.
meaning.links: How links in the text are marked: both (the rest: the accent and an underline), coloured (the accent, underlined only under the pointer) or underlined (the ink with a quiet underline). Not set, a style with soft marks them underlined, and an export leaves it out.
meaning.grainlevel: Strength of the grain, 1 to 10. 4 is the rest. Only with grain.
meaning.vignette: A darkening at the page's four edges, as a screen's glass has.
meaning.vignettelevel: Strength of the vignette, 1 to 10. 2 is the rest. Only with vignette.
meaning.vignettereach: How far the vignette reaches in from the edges, 1 to 6. 3 is the rest. Only with vignette.
meaning.pictures: How every image on the site is shown: plain as published, bw, sepia, duo (the pair's paper and ink), accent (paper and accent, a duotone), halftone (printed dots), dither (coarse two-colour pixels), grain (film grain), hidden (no images; each article picture becomes a line that shows it).
meaning.picturehover: The picture effect lifts under the pointer and the real colours show. No effect when pictures is plain or hidden.
meaning.alternates: Inter's alternate letters: the one with a longer flag, round quotes, commas and apostrophes. Only while the interface face is Inter; the article keeps its own face's letters.
meaning.soft: The reading text is one step softer than the ink (the secondary rung); headings and bold words keep the ink. How links are marked is links.
meaning.picturedim: Pictures are dimmed a little on the dark side. Applies to plain, bw, sepia and grain.
meaning.picturefade: The article's top picture fades out toward its bottom and sides, into the paper. Not with hidden pictures.
meaning.pictureframe: Pictures wear a frame: a mat in the fields' colour, and with lines a line around it. Off, a picture stands on the paper with its corner alone.
meaning.darkground: By day, the ground around the page takes the style's night colours while the page stays light: the rails and the space around the paper. On other themes, the footer. Nothing changes by night.
meaning.hairlines: Every line at half a pixel: the cards' edges, the fields, the frame and the dividers thin to a hairline. Only with lines.
meaning.tint: The accent colour by name, used for links and the primary button. colours.accent overrides it.
meaning.scope: Legacy. The theme always applies paragraph settings everywhere.
meaning.unlinked: true when the light and dark colours were set independently; false lets one side follow the other.
meaning.effects: The extras' details, one object per effect (title, serif, arrival, cardlight, moving, button, pattern, guides, tint, aurora, pointer, dividers, topline, picglow), each holding only the details that differ from their rest; the effect's own switch is its flat pick (titlefinish, headitalics, headarrival, cardlight, buttonfinish, toppattern, guides, greytint, pageglow, movinglight) or, for the last four, its look.
meaning.roles: Typography by role. head: titles and headings. read: article body. quote: block quotes. kicker: the category line under a title. small: dates, tags, captions, the author line. comment: the comment thread. ui: the interface. title: section titles in the rail and archive. Each role takes face, weight, size (px at desktop width), tracking (m25 to p25, letter spacing in per mille steps, default is none), words (word spacing, same steps), caps, italic, leading. head and kicker also take align (default, the theme's own start; center; right) and colour (ink, the rest; accent; own, the well colours.<side>.head or .kicker). members are named sub-groups of a role that may take their own size, weight, caps and tracking, and under head also align, so the headings inside an article (sub) can stay left under a centred title; a member left out follows its role.
meaning.colours: The style's own paper (page background), ink (text) and accent (links) per side, as hex; also, since 2026-09-26, button (the filled buttons), head and kicker (the roles' own colours, with roles.head.colour or roles.kicker.colour own), ground (the page around the paper) and lift (what stands on the paper: menus, buttons, filled boxes). Every other colour is mixed from these. Ink on paper must reach 4.5:1 and accent on paper 3:1 on both sides.

rules: Send only the keys you want to change from the base; a smaller record is a better record.
A first visit opens on the dark side, so design the dark colours first and check both.
Contrast: ink on paper at 4.5:1 or better, accent on paper at 3:1 or better, on both sides.
A strength key (line, scan, fill, glowlevel, grainlevel, vignettelevel, vignettereach, softlevel, quietlevel, framewidth, dotsize, dotlevel) does nothing unless its switch is true.
Pick fonts from the listed ids only; the theme ships no others.
To try a record without publishing it, open the site at /#style= followed by the base64url of the record JSON.
